caption: Send colour: the palette's colour sent by name to the far side of the graph, where the wave masks it
why: Colour wires cross a graph as much as number wires do. Send colour and Receive colour carry a colour by name instead: whatever feeds a Send colour named paint comes out of every Receive colour named paint.
Its neighbours: Send and Receive for numbers; Knot colour to route a colour wire; sub-graphs to hide wiring.
steps: A scrolling **Palette** colour goes into the Send colour's **in**.
**name** is paint: the Receive colour named paint gives that colour.
There it is masked by a **Wave** (a **Mask**) and goes to the **Output** - one colour wire that is never drawn.
Both nodes vanish when the graph compiles.

try.label: Another name
try.text: name brush: the Receive colour is still called paint and no longer finds it - the node says so and the build waits.
